children: Gold is flat in the early Asian session, trading just below the psychologically-important $4,000-a-troy-ounce level. The precious metal could be weighed as renewed rise in oil prices are reviving inflation concerns, says Kudo's Konstantinos Chrysikos in commentary. "Escalating tensions in the Middle East have raised the risk of energy supply disruptions and damage to infrastructure, lifting crude and strengthening expectations that interest rates could continue to rise," he adds. A higher interest-rate environment typically pressures nonyielding assets such as gold. Spot gold holds steady at $3,994.88 an ounce.(megan.cheah@wsj.com)
